essence: Fire-seat triangle on the left palm — fire-lettered, wind-fanned.
Seed burned in hand and heart by the muttering-absorbed true one.
Śambhunātha's demo credited; the proof singled out.
Grace-joining of the seed; brilliance frees even the immobile.
Mastery in, proof out: only the self-known master.
Free exempt (shaken-off, conductless, knower); bound receive seen-proof rite.
Knowledge self-proved, wanting no further fruit.
Fruit-effected practice (Siddhāmata) or the proof-joining balance test.
Twice divinely attested: Tantrasadbhāva told, Pūrvaśāstra hinted.
Five śakti-signs: bliss, uprising, tremor, sleep, whirling.
Uprising through lightness from hidden body-grasp; earthen chief demoted.
Levitating rite nested in the full sequence.

rasa.dominant: adbhuta with vīra weight (wonder at visible proof; the guru's resolve to demonstrate)
rasa.sthayibhava: vismaya (astonishment at the burned seed) settling into dhṛti
rasa.justification: The ahnika stages marvels — seed sterilized, body lightened, master proven — and each marvel steadies the doubter; the guru's resolve to show (not merely tell) carries the energy, wonder carries the conviction.

sections.SUMMARY: Confidence-initiation for the deluded. The fire-seat triangle blazes on the left palm — fire-lettered, wind-fanned. A little seed, taken and burned in hand and heart alike by the muttering-absorbed true one, is crushed by the fire-kindled phaṭ-series into seedlessness, unfit to fruit. Roasted beyond sprouting, it proves the burning of mala-and-māyā karmas by mantra-meditation-rite force. The seedlessness-proof came from gracious Śambhunātha. The seed is still joined by guru-grace, for brilliant initiation frees even the immobile. Only the self-known master of muttering, offering, worship, and meditation gives proof-bearing initiation. The shaken-off, conductless, and knower are exempt; the conduct-bound perform the seen-proof rite. The conductless need no proof: knowledge proves itself and wants no further fruit. Meditation-and-rest are fruit-effected, says the Siddhāmata — or the proof-joining balance test serves. Tantrasadbhāva tells it, Pūrvaśāstra hints it, both from the Lord. Five signs — bliss, uprising, tremor, sleep, whirling — grade śakti. Uprising rides lightness from hidden body-grasp; the earthen chief-body yields chiefness. The levitation-mantra, the disciple visualized afloat, then the remaining rites as before. Told: the proof-giving balance initiation.
sections.FUNCTION: Establishes proof-bearing initiation as the answer to deluded doubt: the burned-seed demonstration (hand and heart, mantra-fired) transfers sterility to mala itself; Śambhunātha's grace authorizes it; competence gates it; the free are exempt from it; the balance test doubles it; canon and śakti-signs frame it — closing with the levitation rite nested in the full sequence.
sections.KEY TERMS: sapratyayā dīkṣā (proof-bearing initiation); mūḍhajana (the deluded, Māyā-swayed); trikoṇa vahnisadana (triangle fire-seat); savya kara (left hand — grammar over secondary); bīja (seed-demo); phaṭkāradhoraṇī (unbroken phaṭ-series); nirbījatā (seedlessness); nirbījapratyaya (seedlessness-proof); mala-māyā-karman (three malas as karma); śambhunātha (Kulaguru source); yojanā (joining); sthāvara (the immobile, freed); japa-homa-arcā-dhyāna-siddhatva (fourfold mastery); avadhūta/nirācāra/tattvajña (three exempt); sācāra (the conduct-bound addressee); siddhāmata (cited authority); tulāśuddhiparīkṣā (balance-purity test); tantrasadbhāva and śrīpūrvaśāstra (dual canon); pañca śakticinhāni (ānanda, udbhava, kampa, nidrā, ghūrṇī); laghubhāva (lightness); dehagrahatirohiti (body-grasp concealment); bhāvilāghava-mantra (forthcoming-levitation mantra); samutpluta (floated-up disciple).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Āhnika 20 belongs to the Tantraloka's specific-initiation arc (a18 concise, a19 death-moment, a21 absent-initiate, a22 Vaiṣṇava-conversion, a23 teacher-consecration): the proof-demonstration for doubters. Cross-links: a18 (concision kin, same arc); Mālinīvijaya (śakti-signs, samāveśa ladder); Siddhāmata (fruit-dictum); Tantrasadbhāva + Pūrvaśāstra (canon); Agni Purāṇa ekatattva (initiation kin); a10 (tulā-adjacent Tantrasara rite kin).
sections.EXPLANATION: The ahnika runs: (1) charter — confidence for the deluded; (2–4) the fire-seat imagined, the seed burned in hand-and-heart, seedlessness defined; (5–7) transfer to mala, Śambhunātha's demo, grace-joining with boundless range; (8–10) competence law, three exemptions, knowledge self-proved; (11–12) Siddhāmata dictum with balance alternative, dual canon attestation; (13–15) five śakti-signs, levitation mechanism, levitation rite nested in the full sequence; (16) colophon — the proof-giver told.
sections.BOUNDARY: Savya kept left (grammar; Pradipaka's 'right' recorded as secondary slip). Dehagrahatirohiteḥ read ablative hetu (genitive considered, convergent).
